text:
Sara: Heads-up, found a weird edge in the reranker eval — the new int8 quantized cross-encoder looks fine on avg NDCG@10 but drops hard on very short queries (<=3 tokens).
Miguel: interesting, did you check tokenization/truncation artifacts?
Sara: yeah, first thing I looked at. The short queries are getting different token splits between the distil-tok we used for training and the production tokenizer. e.g. 'C++ tutorial' -> ['C', '++', 'tutorial'] vs ['C++', 'tutorial'] on the other.
Darren: that can change BM25 candidates and thus reranker input distribution. Do we have a quick script to bucket by query length & tokenizer mismatch?
Anika: I ran a simple split yesterday, here's the snippet I used in the eval harness:
```python
# compute mismatch rate per query length
for q in queries:
    t1 = tok_train.tokenize(q)
    t2 = tok_prod.tokenize(q)
    mismatch = len(t1) != len(t2)
```
Miguel: can you paste the numbers?
Anika: mismatch rate for length<=3 was ~18%, for length 4-8 ~4%, for >8 <1%. NDCG@10 delta (quantized vs fp16) for <=3 queries: -0.12 absolute. overall delta: -0.01.
Sara: that's massive on the short slice. Could explain the customer-facing regression we saw on chat search.
Darren: is it just tokenizer or also truncation? maybe we pad/truncate docs differently in production.
Anika: both. Production trimming happens at token-level after concatenation: `[query] + [sep] + doc` truncated to 256 tokens. For short queries, the doc receives more tokens and often cuts off the most relevant span.
Sara: hypothesis: mismatch+truncation biases the candidate set and reranker sees fewer helpful doc tokens -> lower scores.
Miguel: actionable: 1) rerun eval with tokenizer normalized to prod for both train/serving; 2) run ablation removing truncation by using sliding windows for doc passages; 3) bucket metrics and run bootstrap significance for each bucket.
Darren: agree. Also check quantization sensitivity: maybe int8 maps certain token embeddings to low precision and the issue surfaces when the encoder sees fragmented tokens.
Anika: I re-ran a small experiment: keep fp16 encoder + int8 linear head, and the short-query drop reduced from -0.12 to -0.04. So head quantization is a large contributor.
Sara: good find. So it's both tokenizer/truncation and head quantization. We should capture both in the model-criteria checklist for onboarding.
Miguel: can we compute per-query significance? I suggest bootstrap on queries for NDCG@10 and MRR. Use 10k resamples, report 95% CI. Example command I used:
```
python eval/bootstrap_metrics.py --metric ndcg@10 mrr --resamples 10000 --buckets query_len:1-3,4-8,9+
```
Darren: also include effect size (Cohen's d) per bucket; small p-values with tiny effect sizes are noisy.
Anika: run queued, ETA ~25m. Also logging the top 20 failed queries where quantized model scored worse by >=0.5.
EVA-bot: Test run completed: bucket ndcg@10 deltas (quant vs fp16): 1-3: -0.118 (95% CI [-0.145, -0.091]), 4-8: -0.009 (CI [-0.017, -0.001]), 9+: +0.002 (CI [-0.005, +0.009]). p-values (bootstrap): 1-3 p<0.001, others not significant.
Sara: okay that's convincing. Next steps? I propose: rollback int8 head for now, add tokenizer harmonization in the eval pipeline, and add per-bucket checks to the PR gating.
Miguel: +1. Also document mitigation: (a) normalize tokenizers, (b) move to passage-level candidate generation to avoid truncation hits, (c) selective higher-precision for head when queries length<=3.
Darren: can we implement a cheap rule: if query token count <=3, force head to fp16 at inference time? Might be operationally cheap since it's a per-request routing decision.
Sara: yep we have routing hooks in serving. I'll open a tiny RFC with perf estimates.
Anika: I'll attach the failing query list and a short repro script to the RFC.
EVA-bot: RFC created: /rfc/2026-03-tokenizer-truncation-mitigation, PR created: infra/serve-routing#482.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary for routing change on staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
Miguel: thanks team. Let's also add a line in the model-onboarding checklist to stress-test short queries with tokenizer parity and head precision matrix.
Sara: adding that now. :white_check_mark: 
Darren: nice catch. this would've been invisible if we only looked at aggregate ndcg.
Anika: learned: always slice metrics by query patterns and tokenization mismatch.
Sara: thread summary: short-query regression driven by tokenizer mismatch + head quantization + truncation; mitigations: tokenizer parity in eval, selective fp16 head for short queries, passage-level generation; actions: RFC + staging canary + update onboarding checklist.
